Add Storybook with MSW-backed stories for client unit tests

Stories declare API scenarios in parameters.msw using the typed handler builder
split out of the node-only mock server, so stories and vitest share handlers.
Handlers are named so they merge: appHandlers answers the requests every page
makes, and a story replaces one by name. Like the unit server, Storybook's
worker answers an unmocked /api/ request with Galaxy's 500, and the story fails.
useStoryMount() mounts composed stories in unit tests with the same handlers
and unmounts them after each test.

Vitest is split into test projects: unit (the existing happy-dom config, still
what pnpm test and CI run) and storybook (every story as a Chromium test via
Playwright and Storybook's Vitest addon, with play functions as interaction
tests). test:browser runs the browser project. adaptViteConfig() is shared by
Storybook and the browser project.

Add infrastructure for recorded client API fixtures

ClientFixtures.capture records verbatim server responses into
client/src/api/__fixtures__, named by OpenAPI path, method and scenario,
asserting each capture's purpose first. GALAXY_TEST_CLIENT_FIXTURES selects
the mode (unset, update, rebuild, check); integration CI checks, and the
integration and unit workflows also run on fixture-only changes.

The comparator tolerates encoded ids, UUIDs, datetimes and server URLs by
pattern and treats everything else as significant. Id cross-references
must stay one-to-one within an entity (history_id, id beside model_class
History or src hda, a url's ids), since encoded ids from different tables
collide on a fresh database. Per-fixture volatile and open (subset) paths
cover the rest.

apiFixture(path, method, scenario, status?) loads a recorded response typed
from GalaxyApiPaths. Unit tests fail on fixtures whose operation left the
OpenAPI schema, fixtures nothing loads or no capture writes, non-literal
apiFixture arguments and references to fixtures that don't exist.
